Press Release:


Eskom Coal Contract - OPTIMUM TWO
Carte Blanche follows up on its explosive investigation into how state-owned power utility Eskom awarded a controversial coal supply contract to a Gupta-linked company.


Script:


Optimum Two Final script for TX Saturday 18th June 2016

Commentary One
This was the document that caused all the trouble on Carte Blanche last Sunday. Signed by Eskom’s Matshela Koko, it revealed half a billion rands prepayment for an emergency coal order from Eskom to Tegeta Resources- a company in which the Guptas have the largest stake and Duduzane Zuma has a significant interest

Peter
I don’t think anyone was more surprised by that document than I was. That wasn’t a smoking gun it was a red hot barrel of a rifle

Commentary Two
Cadiz mining director Peter Major was shocked to see Eskom prepay an emerging company only a few days before they took over Optimum mine

Peter Major
Eskom’s job is to generate electricity not funding start ups or companies in trouble or that have a big dream

Commentary three
Our story explained how Optimum mine that feeds Hendrina power station with coal, had run into financial trouble under its previous owners Glencore. They were losing millions each day, but Eskom refused to alter their contract that expires in 2018. So Glencore put the mine in business rescue and in December Tegeta bought the mine. The big question was how did this Gupta company afford to pay R2.1 billion for the mine and the document suggested that Eskom had given them a helping hand.

After the story various mining insiders came forward

former mining exec
If you try and get money out of them – even if it is one rand you wont get it. For us in the industry the pain was that you had now see documentary proof. I don’t know how to put it, its unbelievable!

Commentary Four
The allegation from our original sources was that Eskom had engineered a coal shortage at the Arnot power station and then pushed aside their regular BEE coal suppliers in favour of Optimum’s new owners- the Guptas. Eskom then gave them a short term contract to divert the coal they were mining for Hendrina, to ARNOT at a lucrative price- and then just extended the contract

Former mining executive
Eskom engineered a scenario where they could justify an emergency they engineered it and they did that to be able to assist Oakbay to take over Optimum



Commentary five
Eskom have vigorously denied these allegations. But for Eskom, the problem wasn’t just that half a billion rand upfront payment, but that Mr Koko seemed to have forgotten that he signed this off to the Guptas Tegeta Resources

Devi
Why did Eskom pre pay Optimum half a billion rand for coal
Matshela Koko
We haven’t. We haven’t
You haven’t?
Koko
We haven’t
Devi
Is it common
Koko
We do it yes …there must be a business case and if there is a business case we do it
Devi
But you didn’t pay OPTIMUM any pre payment?
Motshela
I am not aware of that
Devi
Ok just help me out here this is a document that I have according to this Tegeta has requested some form of prepayment, so what is this?
Koko
You see All the cost plus mines are prepayment, and that is not a surprise to me
Devi
So did you prepay?
Matshela Koko
I suspect that is the case
Devi
Ya but Mr Koko you said no!
I suspect that is the case let me read it
Devi
Have a look but when I asked you you said no …I asked twice.
Matshela Koko
I am not aware that it is paid, but in the event that it is paid it is not unusual
Devi
No Mr Koko we are not moving on from this as quickly as you would like me to move on
Matshela Koko
Lets say I made a mistake
Devi
Not let’s say- You made a mistake!
DEVI
You see one of the biggest mysteries has been how did the Guptas pay the R2.15 billion for Optimum – and now the allegation is this is how they were able to do it, because this is as good as the money in the bank

Matshela Koko
I can’t respond to that That is your version. Here is my version I have a need for coal and I have to secure the quality – in the same way I do with all other mines …when I use the R38 billion rand that is what it is – I pre pay to secure the coal that I need its not unusual

Commentary Six
Eskom must have been concerned. As early as last Saturday evening they began sending out press releases. Then Eskom chairperson Ben Ngubane appeared live on ANN 7 defending the parastatals pre payment as a common occurrence

BEN NGUBANE UPSOUND
This is ridiculous …R38 billion of prepayments

Former mining executive
They are not a prepayment – they are capital investments, it is being made to look like the captive mines are the reason for the high cost when it is a combination of factors including the failure of Eskom to invest in the mines

Commentary Seven
Since the story went out Eskom has painted the allegations as an attack on new BEE mining companies, but our sources claim they are the very people that Eskom has left high and dry with contracts hanging in the balance for months

Devi
Are they under pressure
Sam
A lot! They have been trying to speak to Eskom
Devi
Is it possible that some of these suppliers could they go under
Sam
Yes, most of them could go under.
Devi
So are you telling me that some of the juniors went and borrowed money and have no contract now
Yes, that is what is happening at the moment.

Commentary eight
At ANN 7 they went into overdrive even before the story went out. Oakbay CEO NAZEEM HOWA

UP Sound NAZEEM
So our offer to Carte Blanche was let us come on live this evening, they declined that on the basis that they said the format doesn’t suit them



Commentary nine
On Friday, we met Nazeem Howa at the Oakbay offices and asked him how they paid for the mine

Nazeem
I am very surprised by this question? We did it through a mixture of debt and our own funding

Commentary Ten
But the document signed only days before their payment to the bank suggests Eskom helped the Guptas buy Optimum mine, but they reject that, saying the only reason they were paid upfront was to buy equipment to help them supply the 1. 2 million tonnes of coal to ARNOT.

Devi
The elephant in the room Nazeem is that you knew in advance Eskom would prepay you?
Nazeem
Until Eskom approached us to increase supply there was no discussion of a prepayment
Devi
So you saying no collusion no special treatment
Nazeem
Absolutely and I would love you to prove that

Commentary eleven
Nazeem may have done that for us. Listen carefully to what he has to say about how Tegeta funded the deal.

Nazeem Howa
In December when we closed this deal we needed to fund the deal, and part of the deal was we had to prove funding, so we approached the consortium that were owed R2.5 by Glencore and we said to them, we are purchasing this mine- will you help us fund this mine.

The First option we said to them roll over the debt to the end of the period you are already committed for, keep all the securities in place; Second let us put a billion of cash in – roll over the balance and you keep all the the securities in place, you take the Eskom payment directly – we don’t see the Eskom money and we are sure we will pay you off by the end of the period, third option is give us a haircut and we pay cash up front. They declined all three and said show us what you are going to pay and settle upfront

Commentary twelve
But what intrigues Carte Blanche is what Eskom money is Nazeem referring to. Didn’t he say
They used their own money and debt to finance the mine?

Devi
That was in December last year
Nazeem
Yes
Devi
So in December last year you knew you were going to get a prepayment from Eskom

Nazeem
No we did not

Commentary thirteen
Even as Oakbay and Eskom insist there was no wrong doing, at the very least surely Matshela Koko was curious about why four South African banks had closed Gupta linked accounts shortly before he signed the prepayment in April.

Nazeem
It is unheard of in SA history for all the banks to close your bank accounts. Unheard of!

Commentary fourteen
Nazeem says the banks have given them no reasons for the closure and to our surprise he offered to read the confidential letter Standard bank wrote to them

Nazeem
Inclusive of South Africa’s Companies Act, Regulation 43, Prevention of Organized Crimes Act; Prevention and Combatting of Corrupt Activities Act and Financial intelligence Centre Act, as well as the USA’s Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the UK Briberies Act, prevents us from having dealings with any person or entity where a reasonably diligent and vigilant person would suspect that such dealings could directly or indirectly make us a party to or accessory to contraventions of that law
Devi
What does that mean?
Nazeem
That is the reason they have given us. The next paragraph says that they have conducted enhanced due diligence of the Oakbay Entities and as required by the FICA act and have concluded that continuing with any bank customer relations with them would increase our risk of exposure to contravention of the mentioned law to an unacceptable level
Devi
What are they saying?
Nazeem Howa
They are seeing a risk that we may possibly have done it

Commentary Fourteen
But banks or no banks The Gupta’s are on the hunt for new coal mines. Watch this space

Devi
Why are you talking to us?
Former mining Executive
The industry is facing a danger, what is happening at the moment will kill investment in mining. We want the economy to grow and its not happening because the focus is on one company or narrow interests

THE END 10 57

PROMO One 10 seconder
The Gupta’s are on the hunt for new coal assets. But their latest mine Optimum has been shrouded in controversy. More on our exclusive story from last week

PROMO Two
Last week we revealed Eskom’s half a billion rand pre payment to the Gupta’s Tegeta Resources

Peter
I don’t know how any body in good conscience can sign to give someone an advance of R500 million without finding out why the four banks cut him off.
PROMO Three

PROMO THREE
Oakbay’s Nazeem Howa defends the Gupta linked companies as allegations surface of special treatment by Eskom

Devi
So you saying no collusion no special treatment
Nazeem
Absolutely and I would love you to prove that
